LightPath Technologies Reports Fiscal 2027 First Quarter Financial Results

 

ORLANDO, FL – November 10, 2026 – LightPath Technologies, Inc. (NASDAQ: LPTH) ("LightPath," the "Company," "we," or "our"), a leading provider of next-generation optics and imaging systems for both defense and commercial applications, today announced financial results for its fiscal 2027 first quarter ended September 30, 2026.

First Quarter Fiscal 2027 & Subsequent Highlights:

 

 

●

 Grew order backlog to a record of approximately $132.9 million as of September 30, 2026, up 20% from $110.9 million at June 30, 2026 and up 54% from $86.0 million at September 30, 2025, with approximately $110.8 million requested by customers for delivery within the next twelve months.

 

 

●

 Secured more than $30 million of follow-on counter-unmanned aircraft system (“C-UAS”) orders from July  through October 2026, including more than $19 million of optical assembly orders from a leading C-UAS and defense systems supplier — double that customer’s total for all of fiscal 2026 — and an $11 million infrared camera order from a leading global technology customer.

 

 

●

 Received an order in October 2026 from a key defense customer for over 50,000 optical assemblies for drone camera systems as the U.S. and its allies rapidly scale up drone procurement.

 

 

●

 Awarded a funded prototype agreement under the Department of War’s Critical Low-risk Electro-optic Alternatives for Resilience (“CLEAR”) program to further develop BlackDiamond™ chalcogenide glass and optics as germanium alternatives for defense electro-optic and infrared (“EO/IR”) systems.

 

 

●

 Strengthened imaging systems leadership with the promotion of Michael Amorelli to VP Engineering, Imaging Systems, and the appointment of former Anduril Industries production leader Scott Payette as Vice President of LightPath and General Manager of G5 Infrared LLC (“G5 Infrared”).

 

 

●

 Completed the previously announced sale of the Company’s China subsidiary, LightPath Optical Instrumentation (Zhenjiang) Co., Ltd. (“LPOIZ”), as of October 30, 2026, as a result of which LightPath no longer has facilities or operations based in China.

 

Management Commentary

 

Sam Rubin, President and Chief Executive Officer of LightPath, said: “Fiscal 2027 is off to a strong start, led by backlog, a key indicator of our expected future revenue trends. New orders significantly outpaced shipments during the first quarter, lifting backlog by $22 million to a record $132.9 million, with approximately $110.8 million of it requested by customers for delivery over the next twelve months.

 

 
 

 

“The composition of our revenue continues to be more favorable as well. Revenue grew 38% year-over-year to $20.8 million, and assemblies and modules accounted for 51% of the total, up from 40% a year ago. That shift toward higher-value cameras and optical assemblies lifted gross margin to 41.4%, and we generated positive adjusted EBITDA for the fifth consecutive quarter while more than doubling our investment in new product development.

 

“Demand continues to build in optical assemblies and infrared cameras, two of our three projected growth pillars alongside large defense programs. A leading C-UAS supplier has placed more than $19 million of follow-on optical assembly orders with us since July 1, a leading global technology customer added an $11 million follow-on camera order, and we recently received an order for more than 50,000 optical assemblies for drone camera systems. At the same time, the Department of War selected BlackDiamond™ for a funded prototype agreement under its CLEAR program to develop and commercialize germanium alternatives for defense infrared systems – direct government support for the materials at the center of our platform.

 

“Our focus for the balance of fiscal 2027 is converting this backlog on schedule. We invested ahead of scheduled deliveries during the quarter, building inventory of critical materials and work-in-process and adding manufacturing capacity, including glass fabrication. With a strong balance sheet, a strengthened imaging systems leadership team under Scott Payette and Michael Amorelli, and the completion of our China divestiture in October 2026, we believe LightPath is well positioned to focus on scaling as a trusted, vertically integrated supplier of infrared optics and imaging systems,” concluded Rubin.

 

First Quarter Fiscal 2027 Financial Results

 

Revenue for the first quarter of fiscal 2027 increased 38% to $20.8 million, as compared to $15.1 million in the same quarter of the prior fiscal year. Revenue by product group for the first quarter of fiscal 2027 and the same quarter of the prior fiscal year was as follows:

Assemblies and modules revenue grew 76% to $10.5 million, or 51% of total revenue, as G5 Infrared’s camera and module sales increased on surveillance and C-UAS programs with global technology and defense customers. Infrared components revenue increased 15%, primarily driven by the addition of $1.1 million from Amorphous Materials (“AML”) following its acquisition in January 2026. This increase was partially offset by a decrease in sales to defense customers in Europe due to timing of orders.

 

Visible components revenue increased 19%, reflecting higher sales to industrial customers in Europe as well as U.S. defense customers and distributors. Engineering services revenue decreased $0.2 million, due to timing of certain customer programs.

 

Gross profit increased 92% to $8.6 million, or 41.4% of revenue, in the first quarter of fiscal 2027, as compared to $4.5 million, or 29.8% of revenue, in the prior year period. The more than 1,100 basis point expansion in gross margin primarily reflects revenue mix, as assemblies and modules, which typically earn higher margins, grew to 51% of total revenue from 40% a year earlier.

 

 
 

 

Operating expenses for the first quarter of fiscal 2027 were $10.8 million, as compared to $7.0 million in the prior year period. That increase primarily reflects $3.7 million of higher selling, general and administrative expenses (“SG&A”) – including $1.4 million of higher non-cash stock-based compensation, the addition of AML, which was not part of the prior year period, and IT investments required by defense customers’ cybersecurity standards –  along with a $1.2 million increase in new product development costs as the Company added additional engineering staff. These increases were partially offset by the $1.1 million decrease in earnout fair value adjustments.

 

Net loss for the first quarter of fiscal 2027 improved to $1.7 million, or $0.02 per basic and diluted share, as compared to a net loss of $2.9 million, or $0.07 per basic and diluted share, in the prior year period. The improvement reflects higher gross profit, a lower earnout fair value adjustment and an increase in interest income.

 

Adjusted EBITDA* for the first quarter of fiscal 2027 increased to $1.3 million, or 6% of revenue, as compared to $0.4 million, or 2% of revenue, in the prior year period, reflecting five consecutive quarters of positive adjusted EBITDA.

 

Cash and cash equivalents as of September 30, 2026 totaled $82.9 million, as compared to $93.2 million as of June 30, 2026. The change primarily reflects a $10.1 million investment in working capital, largely advance purchases of critical materials to support customer demand and the Company’s growing backlog, and $2.5 million of capital expenditures, primarily to expand manufacturing capacity, including glass fabrication.

 

Total backlog as of September 30, 2026 was a record of approximately $132.9 million, an increase of 20% compared to $110.9 million as of June 30, 2026 and an increase of 54% compared to $86.0 million as of September 30, 2025. Approximately $110.8 million of the September 30, 2026 backlog is requested by customers for delivery within the next twelve months.

About LightPath Technologies

 

LightPath Technologies, Inc. (NASDAQ: LPTH) is a leading provider of next-generation optics and imaging systems for both defense and commercial applications. As a vertically integrated solutions provider with in-house engineering design support, LightPath's family of custom solutions range from proprietary BlackDiamond™ chalcogenide-based glass materials – sold under exclusive license from the U.S. Naval Research Laboratory – to complete infrared optical systems and thermal imaging assemblies. The Company's primary manufacturing footprint is located in Orlando, Florida with additional facilities in Texas, New Hampshire and Latvia. To learn more, please visit www.lightpath.com.

 

 
 

 

**Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures

 

To provide investors with additional information regarding financial results, this press release includes references to EBITDA and adjusted EBITDA, which are non-GAAP financial measures. The Company calculates EBITDA by adjusting net income to exclude net interest expense, income tax expense or benefit, depreciation, and amortization. We also calculate adjusted EBITDA, which excludes, as applicable: (1) stock compensation expenses; (2) the loss on extinguishment of debt; (3) the effect of non-cash income or expenses associated with the fair value adjustments related to the acquisition earnout liabilities; (4) acquisition costs, including legal fees and due diligence; and (5) the effect of foreign exchange gains or losses.

 

A “non-GAAP financial measure” is generally defined as a numerical measure of a company’s historical or future performance that excludes or includes amounts, or is subject to adjustments, so as to be different from the most directly comparable measure calculated and presented in accordance with GAAP. The Company’s management believes that these non-GAAP financial measures, when considered together with the GAAP financial measures, provide information that is useful to investors in understanding period-over-period operating results separate and apart from items that may, or could, have a disproportionately positive or negative impact on results in any particular period. Management also believes that these non-GAAP financial measures enhance the ability of investors to analyze underlying business operations and understand performance. In addition, management may utilize these non-GAAP financial measures as guides in forecasting, budgeting, and planning. Non-GAAP financial measures should be considered in addition to, and not as a substitute for, or superior to, financial measures presented in accordance with GAAP. A reconciliation of these non-GAAP financial measures with the most directly comparable financial measures calculated in accordance with GAAP is presented in the table below.
